subject: humanities
passage: The steelpan, the national instrument of Trinidad and Tobago, began as a kind of recycling. In the 1930s and 1940s, musicians in Trinidad took steel oil drums that had been ______ after use and hammered their tops into shallow bowls. They shaped each bowl into dented sections that ring at different pitches, so a drum nobody wanted became an instrument capable of playing full melodies.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The text calls the steelpan's beginning "a kind of recycling" and later describes the oil drum as one "nobody wanted." A container that was thrown away after use is discarded, so "discarded" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. "Recycling" and "a drum nobody wanted" show that the drums had been thrown away, or discarded, after use.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes the drums as unwanted objects that were recycled; nothing suggests the musicians bought them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not mention decorating the drums; it says they were unwanted until musicians reshaped them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing says the drums were restored to good condition before the musicians got them; the text says "nobody wanted" them.
